examples.en: Our school holds a song festival next week.
I decided to enter the song contest with my friends.

examples.ko: 그 가요제에서 상을 받은 가수가 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: The singer who won a prize at that festival became famous.
The university song festival is held every autumn.
I was so nervous on the song festival stage.
Who are the judges of this year's song festival?

explain: '가요제'는 노래를 겨루는 대회나 축제예요. 학교, 회사, 동네에서 열리는 작은 행사에도 쓰고, 예전에는 TV 가요제가 인기였어요. 오디션과 달리 가수가 되려는 사람만 나오는 자리는 아니에요.

phrases.en: I'm entering the singing contest this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에 참가한다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you're joining the contest.

phrases.example: 우리 회사는 매년 가을에 가요제를 열어요.
phrases.en: Our company holds a singing contest every autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 준비해서 하는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of those who organize the event.

phrases.en: I was so nervous on the singing contest stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에서 노래하는 무대를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The stage where people sing at the contest.

explain_en: 가요제 is a contest or festival where people sing. It is used for small events at schools, companies and towns, and TV song festivals were once very popular. Unlike an audition, it is not only for people aiming to become singers.

examples.en: On summer nights I tell spooky stories with friends.
There is a scary ghost story at our school.
I heard that story isn't true.

examples.ko: 인터넷에 퍼진 괴담 때문에 사람들이 불안해해요.
examples.en: People are anxious because of a rumor that spread online.

examples.ko: 괴담 영화를 보고 밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I watched a ghost-story movie and couldn't sleep at night.

examples.ko: 할머니께 옛날 괴담을 듣고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I heard an old spooky tale from my grandmother and was startled.

explain: 귀신이나 이상한 일을 다룬 무서운 이야기를 말해요. '귀신 이야기'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요. 뉴스에서는 근거 없이 퍼지는 무서운 소문을 '괴담'이라고 부르기도 해서, '식품 괴담'처럼 거짓 소문에도 써요.

phrases.en: A strange spooky rumor spread on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서운 이야기나 거짓 소문이 널리 알려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a scary story or false rumor spreads widely.

phrases.en: When I hear school ghost stories, I get scared at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소 이름을 앞에 붙여 그곳에서 전해지는 무서운 이야기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a place name before it to mean the scary stories told about that place.

phrases.en: We told ghost stories while camping.
phrases.nuance_ko: '괴담'을 풀어서 말한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say 괴담 in plainer words.

explain_en: Besides ghost stories, news uses '괴담' for scary groundless rumors, as in '식품 괴담' (food scare rumors). In casual talk people also say '귀신 이야기'.

examples.en: The piano melody is very beautiful.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 선율이 쉬워서 금방 외웠어요.
examples.en: The melody of this song is easy, so I memorized it quickly.
I can hear a soft melody from outside the window.

examples.ko: 영화 속 선율이 마음에 오래 남았어요.
examples.en: The melody in the movie stayed in my heart for a long time.
I feel calm when I hear the sound of a violin melody.
That singer's voice flows like a melody.

explain: '선율'은 '멜로디'와 같은 뜻이지만 글이나 감상 이야기에서 더 우아하게 들려요. 보통 '아름다운 선율', '선율이 흐르다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '멜로디'나 '노래'가 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I can hear the beautiful melody of the violin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악을 칭찬할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for praising music.

phrases.en: A soft melody flows through the cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악이 조용히 퍼질 때 쓰는 글 같은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A literary phrase for music spreading quietly.

phrases.en: This song has an easy melody.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선율'과 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 선율 and more common in daily talk.

explain_en: 선율 means the same as 'melody' but sounds more elegant, used in writing and when describing music. It often appears as '아름다운 선율' or '선율이 흐르다'. In daily talk '멜로디' or '노래' is more common.

examples.ko: 그 영화의 속편이 다음 달에 나와요.
examples.en: The sequel to that film comes out next month.
I think the sequel is more fun.
The author is writing a sequel to the novel.

examples.ko: 속편을 보기 전에 앞 이야기를 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: I rewatched the first story before seeing the sequel.
Fans were happy about news of the drama sequel.
The sequel was not as fun as I expected.

explain: '속편'은 앞 이야기가 끝난 뒤의 이야기예요. 영화나 소설에 자주 쓰고, 드라마나 만화는 '2기', '시즌 2'라고 많이 말해요. 반대로 앞 이야기는 '전편'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The sequel to this novel is coming out soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 이야기가 발표되거나 출시될 때 '나오다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '나오다' goes with a sequel being released or announced.

phrases.example: 저는 그 영화의 속편을 기다리고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm waiting for the sequel to that movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞 이야기를 재미있게 본 뒤에 다음 이야기를 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you enjoyed the first story and want the next one.

phrases.en: I watched both the first film and the sequel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞 이야기인 '전편'과 짝으로 써서 둘을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with '전편' (the earlier part) to talk about both together.
phrases.en_equiv: the first part and the sequel

explain_en: 속편 is the story that continues after the first one ends. It is common for films and novels, while for dramas and cartoons people more often say 2기 or 시즌 2. The opposite, the earlier story, is 전편.

examples.ko: 올림픽 시상대에서 메달을 목에 거는 선수의 눈에 눈물이 맺혔어요.
examples.en: Tears welled up in the athlete's eyes as the medal was hung around the neck on the Olympic podium.

examples.ko: 시상대 맨 위에 올라선 선수가 손을 흔들었어요.
examples.en: The athlete who stood at the top of the podium waved.

examples.ko: 시상대에 오른 세 선수가 함께 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The three athletes on the podium took a photo together.
Sadly, I didn't make it onto the podium.
The national anthem played over the podium.

examples.ko: 동생은 언젠가 시상대에 서는 게 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling dreams of standing on the podium someday.

explain: '시상대에 오르다/서다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 대회에서 입상했다는 뜻으로도 자연스럽게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: Our athlete finally stood on the podium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입상했다는 뜻으로도 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also naturally means placing in a competition.

phrases.en: That athlete stood on the podium for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올라서 있는 모습에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the image of standing there.

phrases.en: The athletes waved from the podium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시상대 위에서 일어나는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing something that happens up on the podium.

explain_en: It pairs as '시상대에 오르다/서다' (get onto/stand on the podium). It is also a natural way to say someone placed in a competition.

examples.en: The villagers believed in an old curse.
The witch put a curse on the prince.
The curse was lifted and the prince turned back into a person.
A cursed house appears in this movie.

examples.ko: 팀이 계속 지자 선수들은 저주 때문이라고 농담했어요.
examples.en: When the team kept losing, the players joked that it was because of a curse.

examples.ko: 그 보석에는 저주가 있다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: They say that jewel carries a curse.

explain: '저주를 걸다', '저주가 풀리다', '저주를 받다'처럼 써요. 반대되는 말은 '축복'이에요. 욕과 달리 나쁜 일이 생기기를 비는 무거운 말이에요.

phrases.en: The witch put a curse on the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가에게 저주를 내릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when laying a curse on someone.

phrases.en: The curse was broken by a kiss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저주가 사라질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a curse is lifted.

phrases.en: They say that jewel is cursed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저주를 입은 쪽이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the one affected by the curse is the subject.

explain_en: Common phrases are '저주를 걸다' (put a curse on), '저주가 풀리다' (a curse is lifted), and '저주를 받다' (be cursed). The opposite is '축복' (blessing). Unlike a swear word, it wishes bad things on someone, so it is heavy.

en: to sing together; to sing in unison

examples.ko: 우리 반 학생들이 함께 노래를 합창해요.
examples.en: The students in our class sing a song together in chorus.
At graduation, I sang the school song with my friends.

examples.ko: 내일 공연에서 다 같이 합창할 거예요.
examples.en: We will all sing together at tomorrow's performance.
I can hear the children singing in chorus all the way down the hall.

examples.ko: 다 함께 합창하고 나니 기분이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After singing together, I felt much better.

examples.ko: 목소리를 맞춰서 합창하면 훨씬 듣기 좋아요.
examples.en: If you blend your voices and sing in chorus, it sounds much nicer.

explain: 혼자 부르면 '노래하다', 여러 사람이 소리를 모아 부르면 '합창하다'예요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '같이 부르다'도 많이 써요. '합창을 하다'로도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: We all sing the birthday song together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합창하다'보다 가볍고 일상적인 말이에요. 친구들끼리 노래할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and more everyday than '합창하다', natural when friends sing together.

phrases.en: Our class sang in a chorus at the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합창하다'와 뜻이 같고, 명사 '합창'에 '하다'를 따로 붙인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '합창하다', made by attaching '하다' separately to the noun '합창'.

phrases.en: A choir contest is held at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합창과 같이 자주 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요. 학교나 지역 행사에서 많이 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common noun pairing with 합창, often heard in school or local events.

explain_en: Singing alone is '노래하다'; when many people blend their voices it is '합창하다'. In casual talk '같이 부르다' (sing together) is also common, and you will often hear '합창을 하다' too.
